extracted.intended_audience: State Departments of Transportation (State DOTs), Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), FHWA program staff, transportation planners, and regulatory/compliance staff implementing 23 CFR Part 490 GHG requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for State DOT and MPO establishment of targets, calculation methods, data reporting, and progress assessment for the National Highway System (NHS) greenhouse gas (GHG) performance measure under 23 CFR Part 490.

rubrics_metrics.name: State DOT metric calculation method (fuel-use data)
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA has retained the State DOT metric calculation method proposed in the NPRM. This approach is based on fuel use data that is already collected by States and reported to FHWA, ensuring comparability between State estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA believes this approach provides a more accurate estimate of total fuel use and CO2 emissions than model-based approaches. FHWA recognizes simplifying assumptions—particularly assuming a similar rate of GHG emissions on NHS and non-NHS facilities per VMT—but views that assumption as justified because differences would be largely constant year-to-year and similar across States, providing consistent monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO flexibility in metric calculation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA is preserving MPOs' flexibility to use a range of different approaches in calculating the metric for the GHG measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges technical capability variation across MPOs; MPOs may lack travel demand models or capacity to use EPA's MOVES; some MPOs may calculate tailpipe CO2 emissions on NHS directly. FHWA removed the NPRM requirement for MPOs to report tailpipe CO2 emissions for all roads.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO metric calculation method agreement requirement removed
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA is not requiring the MPO's metric calculation method to be mutually agreed upon by the State DOT and MPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA encourages MPOs to coordinate with State DOTs on data to the maximum extent practicable. If the MPO's method is not specified in §490.511(d), the MPO must demonstrate the method's validity and usefulness in measuring transportation-related CO2 emissions in the system performance report (see §490.107(c)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets must represent transportation network regardless of ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets established by State DOTs and MPOs shall, regardless of ownership, represent the transportation network or geographic area applicable to the measures, including bridges that cross State borders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to targets as specified in §490.105(d) and related paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial target deadlines for GHG measure
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs shall establish initial targets for the GHG measure identified in §490.507(b) not later than February 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other initial target dates in §490.105(e)(1) apply to non-GHG measures; this is the specific date for the GHG measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG performance period schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: For the GHG measure in §490.105(c)(5), the performance period will begin on January 1, 2022 and will extend for a duration of 4-years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent performance periods will begin as described in §490.105(e)(4)(i)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from 2-year target for GHG; required 4-year target
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets established for the GHG measure shall be declining targets; State DOTs are exempt from the required 2-year target and shall instead establish a 4-year target and report this target in their 2024 State Initial GHG Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §490.105(e)(10)(i)(A)-(C) and §490.105(e)(4)(iv) for application to initial reporting periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets for GHG must be declining targets for reducing tailpipe CO2 on NHS
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets established for the GHG measure shall be declining targets for reducing tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to State DOT targets (§490.105(e)(10)) and MPO targets (§490.105(f)(1)(i)), and to joint targets (§490.105(f)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPOs shall establish joint GHG target for applicable urbanized areas
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs shall establish a joint target for the GHG measure for each urbanized area that meets the criteria specified in §490.105(f)(10). The joint target shall represent the performance of the transportation network specified in §490.503(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when an urbanized area contains mainline NHS highways and is overlapped by multiple MPOs; joint target is a single 4-year declining target in addition to MPO-specific metropolitan planning area targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO target establishment options
rubrics_metrics.description: For each performance measure identified in paragraph (c) of §490.105, MPOs shall establish targets for the metropolitan planning area by either: (i) agreeing to plan and program projects so that they contribute toward the accomplishment of the relevant State DOT target; or (ii) committing to a quantifiable target for that performance measure for their metropolitan planning area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This choice applies to MPOs except for CMAQ traffic congestion measures in paragraph (f)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint target single-target and data sourcing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an urbanized area contains mainline highways on the NHS and is overlapped by two or more MPOs, those MPOs shall collectively establish a single joint 4-year declining target for that urbanized area. Only one target shall be established for the entirety of each applicable urbanized area regardless of roadway ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHS designations and urbanized area data shall be from HPMS data 1 year before the State DOT Baseline Performance Period Report is due; the target must be quantifiable; each MPO shall report the same joint target (§490.105(f)(10)(i)-(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting schedule for GHG (State DOT submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs shall submit Baseline, Mid Performance Period Progress, and Full Performance Period Progress Reports on schedules specified in §490.107, with special GHG timing: Baseline Performance Period Report info related to GHG due October 1, 2026 and every 4 years thereafter; Mid Performance Period Progress Report info related to GHG due October 1, 2028 and every 4 years thereafter; Full Performance Period Progress Report info related to GHG due October 1, 2026 and every 4 years thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions are described in §490.107(b)(1)(i), (b)(2)(i), and (b)(3)(i) for the GHG measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting content: GHG metric and supporting values
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs must report the GHG metric and the individual values used to calculate the GHG metric, as described in §490.511(c), for the calendar year preceding the reporting year and provide a description of the data source(s) used for the VMT information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This content requirement appears in the Baseline, Mid, and Full Performance Period reporting elements (§490.107(b)(1)(ii)(H), (b)(2)(ii)(J), (b)(3)(ii)(I)).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO system performance report GHG content
rubrics_metrics.description: For the GHG measure, MPOs shall report: (i) the calculation of annual tailpipe CO2 emissions for the NHS (may include all public roads) for the period between the current and previous system performance report and the reference year; and (ii) a description of the metric calculation method(s) used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When methods used are not specified in §490.511(d), the MPO must include information demonstrating the method(s) has valid and useful results for measuring transportation-related CO2 (§490.107(c)(2)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Initial GHG Report requirement and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs shall submit an Initial GHG Report by February 1, 2024 for the GHG measure in §490.105(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State Initial GHG Report content is specified in §490.107(d)(1)-(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Initial GHG Report contents: targets, baseline, relationships, metric info
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Initial GHG Report shall include: (i) the 4-year target and a discussion of the basis for the established target; (ii) baseline performance derived from reference year data; (iii) discussion of how the established target supports expectations documented in longer-range plans; and (iv) the GHG metric and the individual values used to calculate it for the reference year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §490.107(d)(1)(i)-(iv) for the full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources for State Initial GHG Report (reference year)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the State Initial GHG Report, State DOTs shall use: (i) data published by FHWA for the CO2 factors for each on-road fuel type associated with the reference year; (ii) fuel consumed data meeting §490.509(g) for the reference year; and (iii) VMT data meeting §490.509(h) for the reference year (§490.107(d)(2)(i)-(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mandates specified data provenance and quality for reference-year calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant progress assessment data extraction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Data used for assessing significant progress include: Fuels & FASH data on August 15 representing prior-year performance and reference-year performance; HPMS data on November 30 representing prior-year performance and reference-year performance; and the CO2 factor in §490.509(f) for baseline, prior year, and reference year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements appear in §490.109(d)(1)(v)-(viii) and specify exact extraction dates and data sources for GHG targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when State DOT data not accepted by extraction dates
rubrics_metrics.description: A State DOT's reported data not accepted in Fuels & FASH or HPMS by the specified data extraction date for the GHG measure is a listed condition under §490.109(e)(4)(vi)-(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-acceptance by extraction dates affects significant progress assessments and may trigger 'progress not determined' or other procedural outcomes described in §490.109.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in of new GHG requirements (no 2-year target assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-in provisions apply only to GHG targets and the significant progress determination conducted immediately after the submittal of the 2024 Mid Performance Period Progress Report: State DOTs are not required to establish a 2-year target; FHWA shall not make a determination of significant progress toward 2-year targets for the GHG measure at the midpoint; FHWA will classify the assessment as 'progress not determined' and exclude it from the requirement under §490.109(e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These temporary phase-in rules are in §490.109(e)(6)(i)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial documentation when significant progress not made
rubrics_metrics.description: If significant progress is not made for the target established for the GHG measure, the State DOT shall document the actions it will take to achieve the GHG performance target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is in §490.109(f)(1)(v) and applies to GHG targets found not to have made significant progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of GHG measure to NHS mainline highways
rubrics_metrics.description: The Greenhouse Gas (GHG) measure in §490.507(b) is applicable to all mainline highways on the Interstate and non-Interstate NHS (§490.503(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the network scope to which the measure applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Greenhouse gas and Reference year
rubrics_metrics.description: Greenhouse gas (GHG) is any gas that absorbs infrared radiation; approximately 97 percent of on-road GHG emissions are CO2. Reference year is calendar year 2022 for the purpose of the GHG measure (§490.505 definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies substance counted and the fixed temporal baseline for the percent-change metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG performance measure metric definition (percent change)
rubrics_metrics.description: One measure is used to assess GHG emissions: the percent change in tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS compared to the reference year (the GHG measure) (§490.507(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the official metric used to assess GHG performance of the NHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA posting of CO2 factors (annual)
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA will post on the FHWA website, no later than August 15th of each reporting year, the CO2 factors for each on-road fuel type that will be used to calculate the GHG metric (§490.509(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must use these published CO2 factors for reporting and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fuel sales data requirements for GHG calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fuel sales information needed to calculate fuel consumed for the GHG measure shall (1) represent the total number of gallons of fuel consumed by fuel type; and (2) be based on fuel sales data for the prior calendar year, and reported to Fuels & FASH (§490.509(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies aggregation by fuel type, calendar-year basis, and the reporting system (Fuels & FASH).

rubrics_metrics.name: VMT data requirements for GHG calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual vehicle miles traveled (VMT) needed to calculate the GHG measure shall come from the best available data that represents the prior calendar year and is consistent, to the maximum extent practicable, with data submitted to HPMS (§490.509(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires use of best-available prior-year VMT data and consistency with HPMS submission practices.
